title: Frequent request timed out error
body:
I am getting this error whenever the time is greater than 60 seconds. I tried giving timeout=120 seconds in ChatOpenAI(). 

`Retrying langchain.chat_models.openai.ChatOpenAI.completion_with_retry.<locals>._completion_with_retry in 4.0 seconds as it raised Timeout: Request timed out: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='<redacted-host>', port=443): Read timed out. (read timeout=60).`
 
What is the reason for this issue and how can I rectify it?

> Still driving me batty. Looking at server config gunicorn on azure gthread / gevent worker and thread numbers timeouts, Auzure timeouts etc. Could just be the size of the VM, but I shouldn't need a production level server for testing with 5 users. Getting to the point I think I might just have to re-write in node/js. Anyone have the magic configuration for gunicorn that works as well as the development flask server?

It's common to have to increase the gunicorn timeout when running on prod, their default timeout is too short.

However, from a designing perspective, calling Langchain may take unpredictable times, so a safer solution in this case would implement some sort of queue system (for example using Celery). This way the processing happens in background and you won't have timeout issues with gunicorn.

That said, you can try to increase gunicorn timeout by doing something like `gunicorn --timeout 300 [rest of commands]`

comments.author: participant18
comments.body:
I'm using langchain==0.0.319 and Adding request_timeout=120 to ChatOpenAI() looks working well. 
This means Sometimes participant23 does not return a response within 120 seconds, which causes a retry, and then I could get responds in several calls. 

> What is the reason for this issue?

Actually I don't know but I guess it's because participant23, which is server-side, does not return responses for various reasons: 
 - There is a large number of requests at once
 - Perhaps there is a bug in the server-side program.
 - others..

> how can I rectify it?

Since the root cause of the request timeout is on the server side, this is unavoidable on the client side. The server side will sometimes not respond, and the client side has a responsibility to handle on this scenario. If the retry results in a response, there should be no problem.


In my case, the LLM sometimes does not respond, so I set the response_timeout value to a **_smaller_** value to cause a retry on purpose, so that the LLM will retry when it does not respond, and as a result, I could get the LLM respond properly.

I hope this may be help.

comments.author: participant22
comments.body:
hey guys, i got the same problem today. everything works fine yesterday using langgraph and langchain_participant23==0.2.14 and participant23==1.58.1. but suddenly today all request made with langchain_participant23 result in `Request Time out`. at first i thought it was timeout issue and trying to increase the timeout to 120 as suggested above but to no hope. weird thing is i can connect finely using postman using the same token.

anyway, it got solved by adding parameter participant23_api_base to public participant23 api in case you are using public participant23 endpoint. i don't know it this related or helpful but just want to share.

here are the snippet example :
```
from langchain_participant23 import ChatOpenAI
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo", timeout=600, temperature=0, participant23_api_base="https://<redacted-host>/v1")

```

stumble upon this when trying to figure the langchain_participant23 code and found this :
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/056a416e-f096-4193-b79f-f5e13b7dcc1d)

it seems like trying to find base_url from environment variable and got stuck not knowing where to go, i don't know why because everything works yesterday even without setting up base url but it solved my 6 hour problem
